hou.InterruptableOperation.doc:
hou.InterruptableOperation

Use this class to turn any Python code block into an interruptable
operation.

This class is a context manager which allows the user to press [Esc] to
interrupt a long-running operation, and can also display a progress
percentage in the status line at the bottom of the main window.

You should use this in potentially long-running Python nodes (such as
Python SOP) or shelf scripts. For example if you have code looping over
every point in the input geometry, if the geometry has millions of
points the operation could take a long time. You should perform the

hdefereval.doWorkInBackgroundThread.doc:
This decorator marks a generator function as alternating its execution
between the main thread and a new thread.  The intial code is run in
the current thread until it yields, the next piece of code is run in a
new thread until it yields, and the next code is run in the main thread.
More pairs of worker thread/main thread blocks may be added at the end.

Here is an example:
@do_work_in_background_thread
def func():
    print "initializing in main thread"
    yield

    print "computing result in other thread"
    result = 3
    yield

    print "processing result in main thread", result
